# Residuals

## Passing a residual to a function

A residual reached via move-triggered
narrowing [is passed exactly the same way](#spec.ownership.passing-a-residual-to-a-function.legality-1); nothing here is specific to how the residual
arose.

A parameter naming a struct's own projected type (`Handle.{ .fd }`, or `Self.{ .fd }`
inside `Handle`'s own `extend` block) is ordinary type-matching, available to every
struct regardless of whether it opts into any structural-matching mechanism:

```metel
struct Handle { fd: i64, name: String }

extend Handle {
    fun describe(h: Self.{ .fd }) -> i64 { h.fd }
}

fun main() {
    let handle := Handle { fd = 3, name = "x" };
    Handle::describe(handle.{ .fd });
}
```

A caller must match the parameter's row exactly — there is no implicit truncation at the
call boundary. Passing `Handle.{ .fd, .name }` where `Handle.{ .fd }` is expected requires
the caller to narrow itself first; the call never silently discards `name`.

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.passing-a-residual-to-a-function.legality-1}

A function parameter may name a struct's own projected type; a caller's argument must
match that row exactly, with no implicit narrowing at the call site.

## Aspects on a residual

> **Gap** GAP-OWNERSHIP-004

A residual (`Doc.{ .title }`, the same brand with fewer fields) is a value of its brand, but it is not the whole type, so the
language says which aspects it satisfies. Bound satisfaction and dispatch agree: [a residual satisfies **structural `Copy`**](#spec.ownership.aspects-on-a-residual.legality-1)
(with the `Clone` that `Copy` provides) and keeps the existing [`Drop` dispatch](drop-dispatch.md),
and [**every other aspect that needs an impl is `T0012` on a residual**](#spec.ownership.aspects-on-a-residual.legality-7), whether the whole-type impl is written or derived.

<!-- doc-example: skip reason="fragment: uses bindings (p, d) declared elsewhere, and the last line is a rejected program" -->
```metel
copy struct Point { x: i64, y: i64 }
struct Doc derives Clone { title: String, n: i64 }

let p2 := p.{ .x };           // Point.{ .x }: Copy, because x is
let t := d.{ .title };        // the projection moves the field out
t.clone()                     // T0012: Clone has no impl for the projection (derived: template not yet available)
```

[A hand-written `extend Doc: Clone { … }` does not apply to `Doc.{ .title }`](#spec.ownership.aspects-on-a-residual.legality-2): its body may read any field the residual no
longer has. There is no way to write an impl for a residual itself: a residual has such an aspect only through the rules below.

[`Point.{ .x }` is `Copy` if `Point` grants `Copy` and `x` is `Copy`, whether or not `y` is. A residual of a type that
cannot grant `Copy` (a field is not `Copy`) never is, even if the remaining fields are: the declaration says so, not the
shape. An empty residual `Point.{}` of a `Copy` brand is `Copy`, because the condition holds vacuously](#spec.ownership.aspects-on-a-residual.legality-1).

A type whose `Clone` is written is not `Copy`,
so its projections move like the value itself. The `Copy` rule for residuals is native compiler logic, a named exception: it is to move to the std row template with no change in accepted programs.

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.aspects-on-a-residual.legality-1}

A residual `T.{ .fields }` of a nominal type `T` is `Copy` exactly when `T`'s declaration grants `Copy` and the residual's
**present** fields are `Copy`. It then has `Clone` by the entailment of `Copy`, and its `clone` is the copy. The rule is evaluated over the present
fields: for `copy struct W<T> { n: i64, value: T }`, `W<String>.{ .n }` is `Copy`. An empty residual `T.{}` of such a brand is `Copy`: the condition
holds when no field is present, and a copy of it copies no field.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 7ff6bac2f3c159c0d57a74f61abbe3fcb3000089 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.aspects-on-a-residual.legality-2}

A residual does not satisfy an aspect `A` through a hand-written impl of `A` for `T` (an `extend T: A { … }`), because the body
may read a field the residual no longer has. A bound `T: A` on a residual is `T0012` unless legality-1 or legality-5 applies.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.aspects-on-a-residual.legality-3}

A residual does not satisfy an aspect through a **derived** impl either: the derivation is whole-type, so it does not extend
to residuals. The use-site diagnostic says the derived template is unavailable and does not
name a written impl.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 3f16a69509d7d1be74c6f1e9d7525eaecc9f3cbe -->

<!-- rfc.py:fixtures:start -->
<p class="rigor-backlink"><em>Tested by</em></p>

<!-- rfc.py:fixtures:end -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.aspects-on-a-residual.legality-4}

A residual of a type whose declaration grants nothing satisfies nothing for marker and derivable aspects, as the brand does.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.aspects-on-a-residual.legality-5}

A residual is a value of the same brand, so the brand's `Drop` rule is unchanged: a destructor is dispatched by the row-bounded
rule of [Drop dispatch against a narrowed residual](drop-dispatch.md) and is outside this section.
The total destructuring of a marked dismantling method suppresses the destructor and is separate from that dispatch.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed e2c4f1a81fc5ecffc0944d5212b96f75ac81eb40 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.aspects-on-a-residual.legality-6}

Compiler-computed ownership capabilities (`Discard`) are not impls: they follow the surviving fields of the residual. A partial
move out of a nominal aggregate is legal only when the aggregate is known `Discard`, so a residual of a linear or possibly linear
aggregate does not arise. A structural type (anonymous record, tuple) that holds a linear value narrows as usual and its leftover
class is recomputed from the surviving components.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed e2c4f1a81fc5ecffc0944d5212b96f75ac81eb40 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.aspects-on-a-residual.legality-7}

The error for an aspect a residual does not satisfy is `T0012` at the use site. When a written whole-type impl exists, the note
names it as the cause; when the aspect is derived, the note says the derived template is unavailable.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 3f16a69509d7d1be74c6f1e9d7525eaecc9f3cbe -->


##### Dynamic Semantics Rule {#spec.ownership.aspects-on-a-residual.dynamics-1}

A copy of a `Copy` residual copies its present fields. No absent field is read.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed e2c4f1a81fc5ecffc0944d5212b96f75ac81eb40 -->
